hypothesis.instruction: In MemoryAugmentedLayer.__init__, add two new parameters: self.use_delta_rule (default True) and self.use_gating (default True). In the forward method, modify the memory write operation to use a hybrid update: compute write_residual via memory_write attention, then apply gating: memory = memory + gate * write_residual where gate = sigmoid(gate_proj(write_residual)). Add a new learnable gate_proj linear layer initialized to zeros. Also add a delta parameter alpha for the update: memory = memory + alpha * gated_write_residual. Add config options num_mem_heads to RMCAConfig if not present.

hypothesis.hypothesis: RMCA-Gated will improve EM accuracy by implementing a more sophisticated multi-gate mechanism that separately controls memory read, write, and forget operations for better information regulation.
hypothesis.rationale: Implementing human_directions item #18 (RMCA-Gated). Hyperparameter tuning has been attempted (warmup_ratio sweep in current config shows 3 values explored, lr set to 0.01 with base_model llama). Since multiple architectural variants (RMCA-Hybrid, RMCA-Delta) have been tried with mixed results and item 18 is a pending human suggestion with highest priority, implementing the RMCA-Gated architecture change takes precedence over further hyperparameter tuning.
hypothesis.instruction: In MemoryAugmentedLayer.__init__(), replace the single scalar memory_gate parameter with three separate learnable gate parameters: memory_read_gate (controls read strength), memory_write_gate (controls write strength), and memory_forget_gate (controls how much old memory to retain). Apply these gates in the forward() method: read_residual = memory_read_gate.sigmoid() * read_residual, write_residual = memory_write_gate.sigmoid() * write_residual, and memory = memory_forget_gate.sigmoid() * memory + write_residual. Initialize all gates to 0.5.

experiments.description: Adding deep supervision with auxiliary retrieval losses at intermediate memory layers will improve EM accuracy by providing stronger gradient signals that guide memory states to encode task-relevant key-value information.

hypothesis.hypothesis: Adding deep supervision with auxiliary retrieval losses at intermediate memory layers will improve EM accuracy by providing stronger gradient signals that guide memory states to encode task-relevant key-value information.
hypothesis.rationale: Implementing human direction item #15 (Deep supervision). This is an architectural change, but follows human priority over hyperparameter tuning. Deep supervision is a well-established technique that adds auxiliary loss signals at intermediate layers to improve gradient flow and prevent vanishing gradients in deep recurrent memory architectures.
hypothesis.instruction: Add deep supervision by: 1) In MemoryAugmentedLayer.__init__, add an auxiliary projection layer (nn.Linear(hidden_size, n_values)) for memory state classification. 2) In MemoryAugmentedLayer.forward(), after memory write operation, compute auxiliary loss by projecting memory state and comparing to target values (use labels from kwargs). 3) In RMCABase.forward(), accumulate auxiliary losses from all layers and add weighted auxiliary loss (0.1 * sum) to main loss. 4) Add config parameter 'aux_loss_weight' default 0.1 to RMCAConfig. 5) Ensure auxiliary loss only computed on segments with labels.
